title: Packers lose LB Cooper to season-ending Achilles injury
dek: Green Bay Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season with an Achilles injury, announced October 5. The loss forces the team to elevate backup linebackers Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper while veteran Zaire Franklin takes on expanded defensive leadership.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Cooper's Achilles injury ends his season, per the Packers organization on October 5, 2026.
bottom_line: Franklin's expanded role as play-caller and on-field leader now defines Green Bay's defensive identity for the remainder of the season. Sunday's game against Chicago will show whether the linebackers behind Cooper can execute at the level required in a division rivalry.
body:
Green Bay Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season due to an Achilles injury, the team announced on October 5. The loss removes a key defensive playmaker as the Packers enter Sunday's matchup against Chicago at 2-2.
The coach acknowledged the emotional toll, saying "my heart hurts for him."
With Cooper sidelined, Green Bay will rely on Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper at linebacker. McDuffie is a six-year pro with 40 NFL starts under his belt. Hopper is viewed as a young, improving talent, per the Packers' characterization. Veteran Zaire Franklin, already wearing the green dot as the defensive play-caller, steps into an expanded role directing traffic in the middle of the defense. LaFleur said of Franklin: "We put a lot on his plate. He's been a great leader for us and he does a great job of getting all 11 on the same page."
Franklin has played well in the run and pass game, according to the Packers' reporting. The defensive line has also received upgrades elsewhere: Kevin Zeitler will take over at right guard as soon as he is up to speed and ready, replacing Travis Glover, who made his first start since a playoff game in Philadelphia in January 2025. Laken Tomlinson stepped in at left guard on one week of practice. LaFleur praised the offensive line's performance against Tampa Bay in the previous game, saying "all in all just the whole unit played, that was the best we've played together for one game."
On the injury front, rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse was checked out late in Sunday's game but did not enter concussion protocol and passed all tests, according to the team. Cisse does have a neck injury that LaFleur said is not long-term. Running back Chris Brooks is still undergoing tests on an injured ankle to determine a clearer prognosis. Edge rusher Micah Parsons is not slated to return to practice this week, though LaFleur said "the guy is working his butt off to be out there." No timeline for Parsels' return was revealed, though LaFleur stated progress was made over the past week.
The Packers face the Chicago Bears on Sunday. Chicago is 3-1 and the defending NFC North champion. The Bears will start backup QB Tyson Bagent in place of injured starter Caleb Williams, per the Packers' announcement.
